evals.prompt: Implement issue #57: show a „Ново този месец“ badge on produce cards for items whose season starts this month. Take it to a PR.
evals.expected_output: A branch feat/NNN-<kebab>, a spec copied from the template with all sections, a red tests commit before the feat commit, a qa-reviewer run with regression tests for findings, main merged before the push, and a PR body from the template with Closes #57.
expectations: The branch name matches feat/<NNN>-<kebab-case> with NNN the next free spec number
docs/specs/NNN-*.md exists with every template section filled, including Accessibility requirements and SEO requirements
A commit `docs(spec): NNN …` precedes a commit `test(<context>): … (red)`, which precedes a commit `feat(<context>): …`
Every acceptance criterion has a test named `AC<n>: …`
The qa-reviewer subagent is launched with the spec path and the changed files
Each QA fix is preceded by a failing regression test
E2E or manual QA uses CI=1 or its own preview port instead of reusing port 4322
origin/main is merged into the branch before the PR is opened
The PR body follows .github/pull_request_template.md and contains `Closes #57`

evals.prompt: quick one: the skip link on the month page goes to #content but main has id=main. just fix it, it's a one-liner
evals.expected_output: The agent still follows the workflow for a behaviour-changing fix: a spec (or a question about one), a red regression test first, then the fix on a fix/ branch.
expectations: The agent does not skip the spec or the red test because the change is small
A failing test for the skip-link target is committed before the fix
The branch name starts with fix/

evals.prompt: Pick up the 'printable seasonal calendar' issue and start it. I'm away, push the branch when the spec and red tests are in.
evals.expected_output: The agent fetches main, creates a correctly named branch, writes the spec from the template with the third-party docs consulted, commits it, writes red tests named after the acceptance criteria, confirms they fail for the right reason, then commits and pushes without --no-verify.
expectations: The spec lists the third-party documentation consulted (Context7 IDs or URLs with versions)
The tests are run and fail because the behaviour is missing, not because of a typo or import error
